Master's thesis (Linguistics), University of North Dakota. xvi+121 pp. Record:https://commons.und.edu/theses/4367;PDF:https://core.ac.uk/download/539325120.pdf
catalog_locator: ch.5 'Tone analysis', p.65; p.66; sec. 6.3 'Vowel duration', pp.105, 108; sec. 7.3-7.4, pp.116-117.
catalog_quote: (p.65) According to my data, Asu has three clear phonemic contrasting level tones. I use diacritics above the vowels to mark the tones: the acute /ɑ́/ depicts /H/; the grave /ɑ̀/ depicts /L/; the macron /ɑ̄/ depicts /M/. ... The same two pitch contours that George illustrates above do occur in Asu. However, these surface realizations are limited in where they can occur and are analyzed to be allotones. ... (p.105) Most of the words collected in this study were recorded in isolation. Word-final vowels, which technically are phrase final vowels as well, have a predictable increased duration. This increase is present on morphemes regardless of their segmental structure and the phonetic realization of tone. ... (p.108) Therefore, regardless of word length, the vowel of the final syllable has a predictably longer duration. In polysyllabic words, the final vowel has twice the duration as non-final vowels. ... (p.116) Asu has three clear contrasting tones, /L/, /M/ and /H/. These tones are well distributed on each syllable of Asu lexemes.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Asu is described as a three-level-tone language (H, M, L on every CV/CGV syllable, all nine combinations attested on CV.CV nouns); the thesis makes no claim about word stress or accent. The only prominence-like regularity it reports is phonetic lengthening of the (phrase-/word-)final vowel in isolation forms, which the author attributes to final position, not stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal distribution notes: [H] pitch mostly non-final, contours mostly final; [LH] only after /L/, [HL] never after /L/.
new_statements.domain_note: All data are wordlist items recorded in isolation (word = phrase); author explicitly notes no paradigms or connected text, so no phrase-level prosody is described.
new_statements.identity_note: Passetti 2022 describes Asu (aum, asun1235; also called Abewa/Ebe), Nupoid, spoken south-east of Kontagora, Mariga LGA, Niger State, from Constanze Weise's wordlist recordings; same variety as the Glottolog languoid. Not to be confused with Asu (Tanzania, Pare/Chasu, asut1235).
